kicker: Defence & aerospace suppliers · Q2 FY27 margins vs FY27 guidance
title: Defence suppliers kept their margin promises, bar one
dek: Zen (38.2%), Azad (37.9%) and Unimech (39.8%) ran ahead of their margin guidance in Q2 FY27; BEL and MTAR landed on it. Data Patterns earned 23.5% against a 35–40% FY27 guide.

stats.label: Data Patterns' H2 delivery need
stats.note: About half its ₹1,742 cr order book must ship by March to meet guidance; H1 revenue was ₹249 cr.

stats.label: Azad's depreciation in a year
stats.note: ₹21.8 cr vs ₹10.9 cr; profit fell 6% even as EBITDA rose 37% on new plants.

stats.label: Zen's margin, Q1 to Q2 FY27
stats.note: Swung on the simulator vs anti-drone mix; full-year guide stays in the mid-30s.

read: Margins at most suppliers are where management said; the open question is Data Patterns' back-loaded second half.
sources: Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage analysis
notes: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margins are from consolidated results filed on BSE, except MTAR, whose 24.4% is from its Q2 earnings call. Each gap is measured against the midpoint of the company's own guidance on its Q2 call: Data Patterns 35–40% for FY27, Zen 'mid-30s' (35%) operational margin, BEL about 28%, MTAR 24%, Unimech its H1 level of about 38% which it called sustainable, and Azad 32–35%, which is a long-term range rather than an FY27 figure. Astra Microwave and Apollo Micro Systems are left out because neither gave a numeric margin guide. Data Patterns' delivery need is Vantage's reading of the call (about half of a ₹1,700 cr book in two quarters); its order book excludes about ₹956 cr of negotiated orders.
